chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said:

I saw Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when a group of people from Khurāsān had come to visit him. They asked him about going to the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and the rewards therein. He said: My father (peace be upon him) narrated to me that my grandfather (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever visits him, seeking the Face of Allah, Allah will remove his sins as He removes the sins of a newborn whom its mother gave birth to. Angels will accompany him on his journey, flapping their wings over his head, having lined up their wings over him, until he returns to his family. The angels will seek forgiveness for him from his Lord, and Mercy will cover him from the highest part of the sky. The angels will call out to him: 'You are blessed, and blessed is the one to whose Ziyārah you have come,' and he will be protected in his family.

key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (seeking divine pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic accompaniment for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith emphasizes the theological significance of Ziyarat al-Arba'in by linking the physical act of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) to spiritual purification. It highlights the Shia belief in the intercessory role of angels and the divine mercy that accompanies sincere pilgrims, reinforcing the grave as a locus of divine presence rather than mere burial.
